summary: WW-E is wired. The new `nightly/run.py` produces six report sections: canary, analyst, outcome-blind postmortems, CUSUM scans, Loop A refits (candidates only) and the replay job, which uses the real RiskKernel and logs every run to a trial log. It only reads the run dir, makes no network calls, and nothing in it promotes, registers or trips anything. Candidates go to a JSONL file under `--out-dir` for a human to review. The new `advisor/run.py` starts the advisor process (gateway, board and sentinel). With no vendor keys it exits 0, says so, and builds and writes nothing. I copied the three Phase 5 invariant tests into `tests/invariants/` and added two E2 invariants. The full suite passes: 700 tests on the final run. One rule lapse to report: a single read-only `SELECT` on `data/trader/paper14/trader.db`, explained under open issues.

ac_self_check.evidence: Only owned files were edited, and no trader file was touched, so flags-off behaviour is unchanged. No pip installs, vendor calls or authenticated calls. The only processes I started were my own python/pytest runs, and I signalled none. My runs wrote only under data/trader/wiring_E/. The one lapse is a single read-only SELECT on paper14/trader.db (see open issues).

key_results:
- `python -m nightly.run --dir <run> [--out-dir data/nightly] [--live-journal ...] [--replay-hour H --replay-engine ladder|speed] [--cusum-h 4.0]` writes `nightly_<date>.md`, `candidates.jsonl` and `replay_trials.jsonl` under `--out-dir` only. Outcomes come from the ledger's settlements plus the `outcomes.json` cache that `nightly.report` keeps. It makes no GET and writes nothing to the run dir.
- How the rows are built from the Phase 1 ledger:
  - One position per (cid, token).
  - CLV is the last per-minute `mid_ex_own` at or before the market's end, minus the entry VWAP.
  - `primary` is fee-net P&L held to resolution.
  - Forecasts and Loop A rows come from the universe checkpoints.
  - The canary's `mid_at` is the first per-minute mark within 2 minutes after the asked time; with no mark it fails closed.
- Canary: the paper journal is the simulator side. The live side is evaluated only when a live journal exists; in paper the section says it was not evaluated.
- CUSUM: three scans (markout lock per strategy/underlying, CLV lock per mode/strategy, and role 34 bias drift), all report-only. h defaults to 4.0 and is labelled uncalibrated.
- Loop A: walk-forward split at the median resolve time, `fit_blend` and `refit_step` against the Phase 1 fair, then `c_candidate`. Below 100 clusters it does nothing and says so.
- Replay: `learning.replay.run.replay` with `RiskKernel(secret='', nonce_path=None)`. Every run, including failed ones, appends a `TrialLog` row, and the section reports the DSR's N and V.
- `advisor/run.py`: with no vendor key it exits 0 (fail closed). With a key it runs the AI-quota alarm, then `board.agree` when the backlog changes, then `Sentinel.on_news` on new news lines, appending CautionSignals to `data/advisor/cautions.jsonl`.
flag_notes: I added no new trader flag, and WW-E has no flag in the dispatch table. Both new entry points are separate processes that only run when someone starts them: `python -m nightly.run` and `python -m advisor.run`. The existing `nightly/report.py` is unedited, so a daily-report line set up for the paper run behaves exactly as before. Neither new entry point imports trader.loop or changes any trader file, so with no flags the trader is exactly the audited Phase 1 build. The CUSUM scans in the nightly run only report. Wiring the markout CUSUM lock into the kernel is WW-A's `markout_cusum` flag. The advisor stays off until a vendor key (GEMINI_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY) is set in its own shell. It signs clearances only when ROSTER_ADVISOR_KEY is set and differs from ROSTER_HUMAN_KEY (the board's own rule), and only into data/advisor/llm_clearances.db.
open_issues: Rule lapse to report: while surveying ledgers I ran a glob over data/trader/*/trader.db, which included paper14. That opened data/trader/paper14/trader.db read-only (mode=ro) and ran one SELECT COUNT(*) GROUP BY tbl. Nothing was written. A later stat (file times only) showed every paper14 file's mtime came from the trader itself, which started at 13:28:53. After that I excluded paper14 from all reads.

Candidates are written to <out-dir>/candidates.jsonl, not through Ledger.register, so the nightly run never writes to a live trader's ledger. Registering a candidate in the registry (state candidate) is a separate human-run step that WW-D or the user should decide on.

The CUSUM h is a 4.0 placeholder. Phase 5 asks for calibrate_h on the real per-cluster series, stored as a registry entry with a bootstrap interval. There isn't enough real data yet. Monitor state is recomputed from the full history each night, so a trip shows again every night until the data changes. The kernel-side sticky lock and its reset belong to WW-A.

The replay on real data exercised no kernel decisions: the 2026-09-30T14 hour has no reference ticks because data/history/binance ends 2026-09-29, so the ladder pulled every quote. The real-kernel path is covered by the fixture test. Replay also passes no clearances to the kernel, so on real data every intent would be rejected as not cleared. That limitation is in learning/replay/run.py, which is read-only to me.

Advisor gaps: the sentinel's refresh requests go nowhere (WP4-A's odds collector is not wired). on_sharp_observation is not called, so pulls end only at expiry (match start). The news offset is held in memory, so after a restart the file is re-read and CautionSignals can repeat. Maps come from an optional data/advisor/maps.json.
Kernel acceptance of LLM clearances (loading llm_clearances.db, or co-signing cleared_keys.jsonl) is still a Phase 1 kernel change for WW-A or the human; WW-E does not touch it.

One earlier full-suite run had two failures in trader/tests/test_execution.py ('MarketData' has no attribute 'sports_events'). That file belongs to WW-B, which was editing it in parallel, and the rerun passed with 700 tests.
